llm.summary: This skill is mostly about Apple job research, but its included helper can call arbitrary Crawlora API paths and methods with the user's API key, which is broader than the stated Apple-only purpose.

dimensions.detail: Network access to Crawlora is expected for this skill, but arbitrary path/method/body support is not proportionate to an Apple Jobs-only integration and could spend credits or send unintended data to the external API if misused.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact includes an executable shell helper requiring curl and a CRAWLORA_API_KEY environment variable; this is disclosed in the skill instructions, but no separate permission manifest or narrower command wrapper is present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and reference/endpoints.md scope normal use to two Apple Jobs GET endpoints, while the helper's inline usage examples advertise unrelated Amazon, YouTube, and Google endpoints and POST operations.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, background execution, privilege escalation, credential storage, or local data indexing was found; the API key is read from the environment rather than hardcoded.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is limited to Apple Jobs search and detail retrieval, but scripts/crawlora.sh is a generic Crawlora REST helper that accepts caller-provided paths, HTTP methods, request bodies, and an overrideable API base.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. It does not appear destructive or deceptive, but its helper is a broad authenticated Crawlora API client rather than an Apple Jobs-only wrapper. Install only if you are comfortable with agents using your CRAWLORA_API_KEY through this script, and prefer a version that allowlists /apple-jobs/search and /apple-jobs/job only.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Shell and network use are expected and disclosed because the skill documents scripts/crawlora.sh, curl, jq, and CRAWLORA_API_KEY; the concern is mainly the lack of a narrower declared or enforced execution scope.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Confirmed: scripts/crawlora.sh accepts arbitrary API paths and methods instead of enforcing the two Apple Jobs endpoints documented for the skill.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Confirmed: the helper comments include Amazon, YouTube, and Google examples that do not match the Apple Jobs research purpose.
[E1] unexpected: Partly confirmed: outbound API calls are necessary, but caller-controlled paths, methods, and JSON bodies create unnecessary external-transmission and capability-expansion risk beyond Apple Jobs lookups.
